study type: Secondary subgroup analysis of prospective cohort study
cohort: Women with 1 previous cesarean delivery followed by a term vaginal birth after cesarean delivery
finding: The study developed and validated a predictive model for obstetrical anal sphincter injuries during vaginal birth after cesarean delivery, finding that forceps use, vacuum assistance, maternal age, body mass index, previous vaginal delivery, and tobacco use were independently associated with increased risk.
mod_finding: Forceps use and vacuum assistance were independently associated with an increased risk of obstetrical anal sphincter injuries during vaginal birth after cesarean delivery.
